def test_is_sorted():
    # Single element list is sorted
    assert is_sorted([5]) == True

    # Empty list is sorted
    assert is_sorted([]) == True

    # Sorted lists with unique elements
    assert is_sorted([1, 2, 3, 4, 5]) == True
    assert is_sorted([1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7]) == True

    # Sorted lists with duplicates (each appearing at most twice)
    assert is_sorted([1, 2, 2, 3, 3, 4]) == True
    assert is_sorted([1, 2, 2, 3]) == True
    assert is_sorted([1, 1]) == True

    # Unsorted lists
    assert is_sorted([1, 3, 2, 4, 5]) == False
    assert is_sorted([2, 1]) == False
    assert is_sorted([5, 4, 3, 2, 1]) == False
    assert is_sorted([1, 2, 3, 2]) == False

    # Lists with an element appearing more than twice
    assert is_sorted([1, 2, 2, 2, 3, 4]) == False
    assert is_sorted([1, 1, 1]) == False
    assert is_sorted([1, 2, 3, 3, 3, 4]) == False
    assert is_sorted([2, 2, 2, 2]) == False

    # Duplicates appearing more than twice even if list not sorted
    assert is_sorted([3, 3, 3, 1, 2]) == False

    # Negative numbers
    assert is_sorted([-3, -2, -1, 0, 1]) == True
    assert is_sorted([-1, -2, -3]) == False
    assert is_sorted([-1, -1, -1]) == False

    print("All tests passed!")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    test_is_sorted()
